model.name: Dependency / Impact
model.purpose: Define the format-neutral platform contract that lets any adopting Dimension identify, namespace, canonicalize, version, patch, time-stamp, validate, attest, project and retire typed dependency edges and downstream impact assessments, without making any storage format, database or interface canonical and without becoming a platform, registry implementation or authorization point.
model.scope_statement: This split governs record-level and service-level mechanics of the Dependency / Impact mixin: how a dependency edge or impact assessment is identified, placed in a namespace and tenant partition, reduced to a deterministic canonical form and digest across tree-shaped and graph-shaped projections, how change is expressed as versioned patches, how clocks and validity intervals are recorded, how records are validated and conformance claimed, how provenance and custody are attested, and how query, mutation, projection, retention and access responsibilities are delegated. It excludes the dependency type vocabulary, impact scoring semantics, traversal or blast-radius algorithms, and all runtime evaluation, enforcement and audit-trail ownership, which belong to adjacent splits, referenced models or the adopting Dimension.
in_scope: Identifier priority, identifier binding and namespace/tenancy partitioning for dependency-edge and impact-assessment records
Deterministic canonicalization and digest rules for tree-shaped and graph-shaped projections, with mandatory loss disclosure
Version identity, patch grammar, change classes and compatibility signalling for this model's own records
Clock discipline separating asserted event time, edge validity interval and observation/ingestion time
Validation profile, severity handling and falsifiable conformance claims against declared shapes and schemas
Provenance and attestation of who asserted a dependency edge or impact assessment, on what evidence
Interface-neutral query, mutation and projection capability declaration, and delegation of retention, access and audit execution
out_of_scope: The typed dependency vocabulary and impact severity or score scales, which are owned by the adjacent semantics split of WM-XCT-037
Graph traversal, transitive closure and blast-radius computation algorithms
Runtime policy evaluation, authorization decisions and enforcement: this model carries policy references and decision inputs but never acts as a policy decision or enforcement point
Audit-trail record structure, storage and retention execution, which belong to the referenced audit or logging model and the adopting Dimension
Registry or catalogue implementation, identifier allocation services, and namespace resolution infrastructure
Cryptographic key management, signature suite selection and trust-root operation
Build execution, SBOM generation and vulnerability triage, which belong to referenced supply-chain models

boundary_notes.neighbor: Adjacent WM-XCT-037 semantics split (typed dependency and impact classification)
boundary_notes.distinction: This split fixes how a record is identified, canonicalized, versioned and validated; the semantics split fixes what dependency types and impact classes mean. Governance findings here reference a declared vocabulary version but never enumerate or redefine dependency types.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Runtime policy evaluation and enforcement models (policy decision or enforcement points)
boundary_notes.distinction: A dependency/impact record may carry a policy reference and the inputs a policy needs, but evaluation, decision outcome and enforcement remain wholly external. Referencing an evaluator never grants this model evaluation or enforcement semantics.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Audit, event log and observability models
boundary_notes.distinction: This model requires that governed operations emit audit events and names the fields they must carry, but the audit record schema, its immutability guarantees and its retention are owned by the referenced audit model and the adopting Dimension.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Catalogue and registry models (DCAT-style catalogue records)
boundary_notes.distinction: Version chains and registration timestamps align to catalogue vocabulary, but catalogue entries, harvesting and discovery services are not implemented here; this model only declares the version metadata a catalogue can consume.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Software supply-chain models (SPDX, CycloneDX, SLSA build provenance)
boundary_notes.distinction: These are alignment and evidence targets. This model may carry a reference and digest to an SBOM or build attestation as evidence for a dependency edge, but does not reproduce their lifecycle, build execution or vulnerability semantics.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Change management, release and incident models
boundary_notes.distinction: Version and patch rules here govern the dependency/impact record itself, not the approval workflow, release train or incident response process that may consume an impact assessment.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Storage engines and interface protocols (files, relational or document databases, semantic graph stores, MCP or HTTP APIs)
boundary_notes.distinction: All are projections. Canonical semantics live in the abstract record; a projection profile and loss disclosure statement is required for each, and no projection is declared canonical.

sources.title: RFC 8785: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS)
sources.relevance: Defines deterministic JSON serialization (lexicographic property sorting, whitespace removal, ECMAScript number serialization, UTF-8 output) and its I-JSON limits, including no duplicate keys, IEEE 754 double number range and no Unicode normalization.

sources.title: RDF Dataset Canonicalization: A Standard RDF Dataset Canonicalization Algorithm (RDFC-1.0)
sources.relevance: Defines deterministic blank-node labelling and canonical form for RDF datasets, enabling comparison, hashing and signing of graph-shaped dependency projections independent of serialization order.

sources.title: RFC 6902: JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Patch
sources.relevance: Defines the add, remove, replace, move, copy and test operations, JSON Pointer targeting, the test operation as a precondition mechanism, and all-or-nothing patch application.

sources.title: RFC 7396: JSON Merge Patch
sources.relevance: Defines merge-patch semantics where null means removal and arrays are replaced wholesale, and states the format is inappropriate for documents that use explicit null values or need partial array edits.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Defines the date-time profile of ISO 8601 with mandatory seconds, the Z designator for a zero UTC offset, numeric offsets computed as local time minus UTC, leap-second value 60, and -00:00 as the unknown-local-offset convention.

sources.title: RFC 9562: Universally Unique IDentifiers (UUIDs)
sources.relevance: Defines UUID versions 1 through 8 and states that implementations SHOULD use UUIDv7, a Unix-epoch time-ordered identifier sortable as opaque bytes, for new time-ordered identifier needs.

sources.title: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
sources.relevance: Defines shapes graphs, data graphs, focus-node targeting, validation reports containing sh:conforms and sh:result, and the sh:Info, sh:Warning and sh:Violation severity levels with sh:Violation as default.

sources.title: SPDX Specification 3.0.1 - Core Model, Relationship class and RelationshipType vocabulary
sources.relevance: Models a relationship as a first-class Element with required from, to and relationshipType, optional startTime, endTime and completeness, and explicit absence semantics via NoneElement and NoAssertionElement - the closest normative analogue to a typed dependency edge.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Provides Entity, Activity and Agent plus wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, wasRevisionOf and wasInfluencedBy, and the qualified-influence pattern used here for attributing dependency assertions and record revisions.

sources.title: RFC 9535: JSONPath: Query Expressions for JSON
sources.relevance: Defines query expressions, nodelist results and normalized paths as a canonical, testable node-location form, and positions JSONPath as a companion to JSON Pointer rather than a replacement.

sources.title: ECMA-424: CycloneDX Bill of Materials Specification
sources.relevance: Standardises description of components, services, dependencies and compositions, plus lifecycle context, external references, annotations, and claims, attestations and supporting evidence for conformance assertions.

sources.title: RFC 8141: Uniform Resource Names (URNs)
sources.relevance: Defines URN syntax, namespace identifiers and namespace-specific strings assigned and managed consistently by a delegated authority committed to persistence and non-reassignment, and separates resolution, service and fragment parameters from the identifier itself.

sources.title: SLSA Specification v1.2 - Build Provenance
sources.organization: Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) / SLSA project
sources.relevance: Defines verifiable provenance describing where, when and how an artifact was produced, serialized as an in-toto statement with subject digests, a build definition including resolved dependencies, and a builder identity that bounds the trust claim.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Practices for Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Public-authority guidance on identifying, assessing and mitigating supply-chain risk across suppliers, products and services, used here as the criticality-analysis and traceability input that motivates governed dependency and downstream-impact records.

sources.title: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) - Version 3
sources.relevance: Provides dcat:previousVersion, dcat:hasCurrentVersion and dcat:version for lifecycle version chains, dcat:DatasetSeries for grouped releases, and dcat:CatalogRecord with dcterms:issued and dcterms:modified separating resource dates from registration dates.

bundles.name: Format-Neutral Record Contract
bundles.description: The abstract-record layer of the Dependency / Impact mixin: how a dependency edge or impact assessment is identified, placed in a namespace and tenant partition, reduced to a deterministic canonical form and digest, and projected into any concrete serialization with disclosed loss.
bundles.rationale: Dependency and impact assertions are exchanged across SBOM formats, graph stores, document databases and human-readable documents. Unless identity, canonical form and projection loss are fixed at the abstract-record level, digests, comparisons and signatures diverge per format. RFC 8785 and RDFC-1.0 each provide deterministic canonicalization only within their own data model, so the contract must be stated once above both.

layers.name: Identity and Namespace Governance
layers.description: Rules for minting, binding and resolving identifiers for dependency-edge and impact-assessment records, and for partitioning them by namespace, tenant and adopting Dimension.

findings.name: Record identity and identifier priority
findings.description: A dependency edge and an impact assessment are each first-class records requiring a stable identifier that is independent of the endpoints they relate. Identity is bound in strict priority: an authoritative master-system identifier where one exists; otherwise a governed global identifier or IRI issued under a delegated namespace authority; otherwise a UUID (UUIDv7 preferred) or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension. Endpoint references are separate fields, never a substitute for edge identity, and no date, version tag or content digest may serve as the identifier.

answer_data: Primary identifier value and its identifier scheme
Assigning system or authority reference
Priority tier satisfied: master-system, governed global IRI/URN, or locally minted UUID/ULID

questions.text: What authority delegated the namespace under which this identifier was assigned, and what persistence commitment applies?
answer_data: Namespace authority reference
Persistence and non-reassignment commitment statement
Delegation evidence reference

questions.text: How are the source and target endpoints of the edge referenced without collapsing them into the edge identifier?
answer_data: Source endpoint reference and its identifier scheme
Target endpoint reference(s) and identifier scheme
Endpoint resolution status and unresolved-reference flag

answer_data: Alias identifier list with scheme and issuing system
Uniqueness assertion per alias
Mapping confidence and reconciliation method

data_elements.name: Record identifier
data_elements.description: The single authoritative identifier for this dependency-edge or impact-assessment record, opaque and free of date-like components.

data_elements.name: Identifier scheme and priority tier
data_elements.description: Coded scheme (master-system key, URN, HTTP IRI, UUIDv7, ULID) and the identity-priority tier that scheme satisfies.

data_elements.name: Endpoint reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a related element, carrying role (source or target), identifier scheme and resolution status; modelled after the from/to structure of a first-class relationship.

data_elements.name: Alias identifier
data_elements.description: A non-authoritative identifier for the same record in another system, with issuing system and uniqueness assertion.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity is expressed as inline fields on the dependency or impact record itself. Materialising a separate identifier document would create a second, competing source of truth and would invite the anti-pattern of a locally operated identifier registry, which this model explicitly excludes. Alias mappings are also inline references; where a real identifier registry exists it is an external system referenced by URN or IRI, not an artifact produced here.

findings.name: Namespace, tenancy and adopting-Dimension partitioning
findings.description: Every governed record belongs to exactly one namespace partition owned by one adopting Dimension, expressed as a URN namespace identifier or an HTTP base IRI with a documented assignment authority. Tenancy is a partition of the identifier and canonicalization space, not an access-control mechanism: cross-tenant references are permitted only as explicit external references with their own namespace prefix, and identifier collision across tenants is prevented by namespace, never by hoping for UUID uniqueness alone.

questions.text: Which adopting Dimension owns this namespace partition, and who is the accountable owner package?
answer_data: Adopting Dimension identifier
Owner package reference and accountable role
Effective date of ownership assignment

answer_data: Namespace form code (URN NID or HTTP base IRI)

answer_data: Cross-partition reference permission rule

Dangling-reference handling policy

answer_data: Resolution endpoint reference held separately from the identifier

Identifier equality comparison procedure

data_elements.description: URN namespace identifier or HTTP base IRI under which record identifiers in this partition are assigned.

data_elements.name: Tenant partition key
data_elements.description: Key identifying the adopting-Dimension partition that owns the record; used for identifier scoping and projection routing, not for authorization.

data_elements.name: Owner package reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the accountable owner package within the adopting Dimension, with the role responsible for namespace stewardship.

data_elements.name: Cross-partition reference rule

It declares a binding; it does not allocate identifiers or resolve them.

artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the namespace identifier it declares, qualified by manifest version; superseded manifests are retained and linked as previous versions rather than overwritten.

layers.name: Canonicalization, Serialization and Projection Loss
layers.description: Rules producing a deterministic canonical form and digest for a dependency or impact record in each supported shape, and the mandatory disclosure of what a given projection cannot carry.

findings.name: Canonical form, digest and artifact integrity
findings.description: Canonicalization is defined per shape family, not per file format. Tree-shaped projections canonicalize under the JSON Canonicalization Scheme, which sorts properties lexicographically, removes whitespace, serializes numbers by ECMAScript rules and forbids duplicate keys. Graph-shaped projections canonicalize under RDFC-1.0, which assigns deterministic blank-node labels. A record's digest is computed over the canonical byte stream of a named shape, and the shape name is always carried with the digest. Because the two algorithms operate on different data models and JCS performs no Unicode normalization, digest equality across shape families is not asserted.

questions.text: Which canonicalization profile applies to this record, and over which shape family was it computed?
answer_data: Canonicalization profile identifier and version
Shape family code (tree or graph)
Named algorithm reference and its version

questions.text: How are impact scores and other numeric values represented so that canonicalization does not silently change their precision?
answer_data: Numeric representation rule, including the string-encoding requirement beyond double precision
Declared precision and unit for each quantitative field
Rejected-value handling for non-finite numbers

questions.text: What digest algorithm and encoding bind this record's canonical form, and how is the binding verified?
answer_data: Digest algorithm name and output encoding
Digest value and the canonical form it covers
Verification procedure and last successful verification reference

questions.text: How are string comparisons handled when the canonicalization algorithm does not normalize Unicode?
answer_data: Declared Unicode normalization form applied before canonicalization, or an explicit statement that none is applied
Text equality comparison rule
Known false-difference risk statement

data_elements.name: Canonicalization profile reference
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the canonicalization profile applied, naming the algorithm and the shape family it covers.

data_elements.name: Content digest
data_elements.description: Digest over the canonical byte stream, carrying algorithm name, encoding and the canonicalization profile it was computed under.

data_elements.name: Numeric encoding declaration
data_elements.description: Per-field declaration of whether a numeric value is carried as a JSON number within IEEE 754 double range or as a string to preserve precision.

data_elements.name: Text normalization declaration
data_elements.description: Declared Unicode normalization applied before canonicalization, or an explicit none, since the canonicalization scheme itself preserves strings as is.

artifacts.name: Canonicalization profile declaration
artifacts.description: Versioned declaration naming, for each supported shape family, the canonicalization algorithm, digest algorithm and encoding, numeric and text handling rules, and the explicit statement that cross-shape digest equality is not claimed.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by profile identifier plus semantic version; each published version is immutable and digest-bound, and supersession is expressed by a previous-version link.

artifacts.name: Record integrity manifest
artifacts.description: Digest-bearing manifest listing the canonical digests of a set of dependency or impact records at a stated point in time, usable as the subject list of an external attestation without this model performing any verification service.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by a minted record identifier; ordered by the manifest's own generation timestamp, never by embedding a date in the identifier.

findings.name: Projection profiles and loss disclosure
findings.description: Every concrete serialization or store is a projection of the abstract record and must be governed by a projection profile that states which elements survive, which are transformed and which are dropped. Known lossy cases are normative examples rather than exhaustive: merge-patch-style documents cannot distinguish a null value from a deletion, arrays are replaced wholesale, absence semantics such as an explicit no-relationship assertion versus a no-assertion statement do not survive into formats lacking that distinction, and stores that normalize timestamps to UTC discard the recorded offset. A projection that cannot carry an element must disclose the loss rather than silently degrade.

questions.text: Which projection target does this profile describe, and which shape family and canonicalization profile does it use?
answer_data: Projection target identifier (format, store or interface family)
Shape family and canonicalization profile reference
Profile version and effective date

questions.text: Which elements of the abstract record are dropped, coerced or restructured by this projection?
answer_data: Per-element disposition: carried, transformed, or dropped
Transformation description and reversibility flag
Residual-information statement for irreversible transformations

questions.text: Is a round trip through this projection lossless, and what test demonstrates the answer?
answer_data: Round-trip classification (lossless, lossy-disclosed, unknown)
Round-trip test reference and last result
Digest comparison outcome before and after projection

questions.text: How does this projection represent an explicit assertion that no dependency exists versus an absence of any assertion?
answer_data: Representation of explicit no-relationship assertion
Representation of no-assertion or unknown
Statement of collapse where the projection cannot distinguish the two

questions.text: How is a partial projection addressed and named so that consumers can tell which subtree or subgraph they received?
answer_data: Node-selection expression and its expression language
Normalized path or canonical location of each returned node
Completeness flag for the returned selection

data_elements.name: Projection target
data_elements.description: Coded identifier for the serialization, store or interface family a profile describes; explicitly non-canonical.

data_elements.name: Loss disclosure entry
data_elements.description: Per-element record of disposition (carried, transformed, dropped), reversibility and any residual information, forming the disclosure inventory.

data_elements.name: Round-trip status
data_elements.description: Classification of the projection as lossless, lossy with disclosure, or untested, with a reference to the evidencing test run.

data_elements.name: Node selection expression
data_elements.description: Expression identifying which nodes a partial projection returned, together with the normalized path form of each returned node.

artifacts.name: Projection profile and loss disclosure statement
artifacts.description: Versioned, per-target statement of the mapping from abstract record to a concrete projection, its complete loss inventory, round-trip status and the representation chosen for absence semantics.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by projection-target code plus profile version; each published version is immutable and digest-bound to the canonicalization profile it depends on.

bundles.name: Service-Layer Operating Contract
bundles.description: The operating half of the governance contract: change control and clocks, validation and conformance, provenance and custody, and the interface-neutral query, mutation, retention and delegation surface.
bundles.rationale: Dependency and impact records are consumed by criticality and supply-chain risk processes where a stale, unattributed or unvalidated edge produces a wrong downstream conclusion. Standards exist for each mechanism - patch grammars, timestamps, shape validation, provenance attribution and build attestation - but none governs a dependency mixin end to end, so the operating contract must bind them together while explicitly delegating evaluation, enforcement, audit and erasure execution outward.

layers.name: Version, Patch and Clock Discipline
layers.description: How a dependency or impact record changes over time: version identity and compatibility classes, the patch grammars permitted, and the separation of asserted event time, edge validity and observation time.

findings.name: Version identity, patch grammar and compatibility classes
findings.description: A record version is an immutable, digest-bound state linked to its predecessor by a previous-version relation, forming an auditable chain. Mutations are expressed as patch documents: an operation-sequence grammar with pointer targets, test preconditions and all-or-nothing application is the default; merge-patch grammar is permitted only for object-shaped subtrees that contain no explicit nulls and require no partial array edits; graph-shaped records use a canonicalized add/remove quad set. Every patch carries the expected pre-state digest and the resulting post-state digest, and declares a compatibility class: additive, corrective, or restrictive (breaking).

questions.text: Which version of this record does the current state supersede, and how is the chain verified?
answer_data: Previous-version reference and its digest
Current version identifier and digest
Chain verification result and gap flag

questions.text: Which patch grammar was used for this change, and why was it admissible for the affected subtree?
answer_data: Patch grammar code and specification reference
Admissibility justification against the null-value and array constraints
Operation list or quad-difference summary

questions.text: What precondition guarded this patch against applying to an unexpected state?
answer_data: Expected pre-state digest or test-operation assertions
Atomicity outcome (applied in full, or rejected without partial effect)
Conflict-detection result

questions.text: What compatibility class does this change carry for downstream consumers of the affected dependency edge?
answer_data: Compatibility class (additive, corrective, restrictive)
Rationale and affected element list
Consumer notification requirement flag

data_elements.name: Version identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of an immutable record state, distinct from the record identifier and free of date-like components.

data_elements.name: Previous-version reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the immediately superseded version, forming the lineage chain a catalogue or consumer can traverse.

data_elements.name: Patch grammar code
data_elements.description: Which change grammar the patch uses: operation-sequence, merge-patch, or canonicalized quad difference.

data_elements.name: Pre-state and post-state digest pair
data_elements.description: Digests of the record's canonical form before and after the patch, used as the patch precondition and result binding.

data_elements.name: Compatibility class
data_elements.description: Declared effect of the change on downstream consumers: additive, corrective, or restrictive/breaking.

artifacts.name: Change set (patch document)
artifacts.description: A single proposed or applied change to one or more records, carrying the patch grammar, the operation sequence or quad difference, pre-state and post-state digests, compatibility class and the requesting agent reference. A change set is a proposal until a separate mutation operation commits it.
media_or_form: structured patch record in any serialization
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by a minted UUIDv7 or master-system change identifier; ordering derives from the recorded submission timestamp and the pre-state digest, never from a date embedded in the identifier.

findings.name: Clock discipline and temporal validity
findings.description: All time values are recorded as internet timestamps with seconds and an explicit offset or the Z designator. Three time axes are kept distinct and are never collapsed: the asserted event time at which the dependency or impact fact holds or held; the validity interval of the edge itself, expressed as a start and optional end; and the observation or ingestion time at which the record was captured by this model. Where the true local offset is unknown but the instant is known in UTC, the unknown-offset convention is used rather than falsely asserting Z. Leap-second values are accepted on input and their normalization must be disclosed.

questions.text: For this record, what are the asserted event time, the edge validity interval and the observation or ingestion time?
answer_data: Asserted event timestamp with offset
Validity start and optional validity end
Observation or ingestion timestamp with offset

questions.text: Which clock source produced each timestamp, and what is its known accuracy or skew?
answer_data: Clock source reference per timestamp
Stated accuracy, skew bound or synchronization method
Trust qualifier for externally supplied timestamps

questions.text: Was any recorded offset normalized or discarded on storage, and where is that disclosed?
answer_data: Original offset as received
Normalization applied and the store or projection that applied it
Loss disclosure reference in the relevant projection profile

questions.text: How is an open-ended or not-yet-known end of a dependency's validity distinguished from an asserted permanent dependency?
answer_data: Open-interval marker semantics
Explicit no-end assertion versus unknown-end assertion
Review-due indication for open intervals

data_elements.name: Asserted event time
data_elements.description: Timestamp at which the asserted dependency or impact fact is claimed to hold, with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Edge validity interval
data_elements.description: Start and optional end of the period during which the dependency relationship is asserted to hold, mirroring first-class relationship start and end times.

data_elements.name: Observation or ingestion time
data_elements.description: Timestamp at which this model captured or last confirmed the assertion; always distinct from event time and always required on a governed record.

data_elements.name: Clock source and skew declaration
data_elements.description: Reference to the clock or system that produced a timestamp, with its stated accuracy or synchronization method.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Time values are attributes of the record and of the relationship they qualify; there is no coherent standalone temporal document. Emitting a separate time artifact would create a second place where event time and observation time could disagree, which is precisely the failure this finding exists to prevent. Clock-source metadata is likewise a reference to an external time service, not an artifact this model produces.

layers.name: Validation, Conformance and Provenance Assurance
layers.description: How a dependency or impact record is checked against declared constraints, how a conformance claim is made falsifiable, and how the assertion is attributed to a responsible agent and supporting evidence.

findings.name: Validation profile, severity and conformance claim
findings.description: Validation is performed against a named shapes or schema graph at a stated version; the outcome is a report stating overall conformance plus individual results, each carrying the focus node, the path, the value, the source constraint and a severity of informational, warning or violation, with violation as the default. Conformance is claimed only against a named profile and a named validation run: a record with no violations under profile A is not thereby conformant to profile B. This model owns the request for validation and the retention of its report; it does not own the validation engine, and it never converts a validation outcome into an authorization or enforcement decision.

questions.text: Against which named validation profile and version was this record checked?
answer_data: Validation profile identifier and version
Shapes or schema graph reference and its digest
Target selection rule used to pick focus nodes

questions.text: What is the conformance outcome, and which individual results were produced?
answer_data: Overall conformance boolean
Result list with focus node, path, value, source constraint and message
Severity distribution across results

questions.text: How does the adopting Dimension treat warnings and informational results that do not block conformance?
answer_data: Severity-to-handling mapping
Accepted-deviation register reference
Remediation due indication

questions.text: Which external engine executed the validation, and what stops its outcome from being treated as an authorization decision?
answer_data: Validating engine reference and version
Statement that execution and enforcement are external to this model
Consumer obligation note for downstream decisioning

data_elements.name: Validation profile reference
data_elements.description: Identifier, version and digest of the shapes or schema graph against which a record is validated.

data_elements.name: Conformance flag
data_elements.description: Boolean stating whether the record conformed under the named profile in the named run; meaningless without both references.

data_elements.name: Validation result entry
data_elements.description: One finding from a validation run: focus node, result path, offending value, source constraint, message and severity.

data_elements.name: Result severity
data_elements.description: Coded severity of a validation result: informational, warning or violation, with violation as the default when unstated.

artifacts.name: Validation report
artifacts.description: Immutable outcome of one validation run over one or more records, stating overall conformance, the profile and engine used, and the individual results with their severities. Retained as evidence; it is not a decision and confers no permission.
media_or_form: structured report record in any serialization
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by a minted UUIDv7 run identifier bound to the digests of the validated records and the profile; ordering derives from the run's recorded completion timestamp.

findings.name: Provenance, attribution and custody of assertions
findings.description: Every dependency edge and impact assessment is an assertion by some agent, derived from some evidence, produced by some activity. Provenance records which agent the assertion is attributed to, which activity generated it, which prior record it was derived or revised from, and which evidence supports it, including references and digests of external supply-chain evidence such as build attestations or bills of materials. Custody records the chain of responsible parties as the record moves between systems. Evidence is referenced by identifier and digest; this model does not verify signatures, evaluate trust or operate an attestation service.

questions.text: To which agent is this dependency or impact assertion attributed, and in what role?
answer_data: Responsible agent reference and agent type
Role in the assertion (asserter, curator, importer, delegate)
Attribution qualifier such as confidence or on-behalf-of relation

questions.text: From which prior record or source was this assertion derived or revised, and by what activity?
answer_data: Source record or dataset reference with digest

Generating activity reference with start and end times

questions.text: What external evidence supports this dependency edge, and how is it addressed immutably?
answer_data: Evidence artifact reference (bill of materials, build attestation, scan output, human attestation)
Evidence digest with algorithm
Evidence type and stated coverage or completeness

questions.text: Which parties have held custody of this record since assertion, and where did responsibility transfer?
answer_data: Custody chain entries with holder, start and end times
Transfer reason and receiving-party acknowledgement reference
Current custodian reference

questions.text: What verification of the supporting evidence has this model performed, and what has it deliberately not performed?
answer_data: Digest-match check outcome, where performed
Explicit statement that signature verification and trust evaluation are external
Reference to the external verifier relied upon, if any

data_elements.name: Responsible agent reference
data_elements.description: Agent to whom the assertion is attributed, with agent type and role, following the attribution pattern for entities and activities.

data_elements.name: Derivation or revision reference

data_elements.name: Evidence reference with digest
data_elements.description: Immutable reference to supporting external evidence, carrying subject digest and algorithm so the evidence can be re-identified without being re-fetched.

data_elements.name: Custody chain entry
data_elements.description: One holder of responsibility for the record over a time interval, with transfer reason and acknowledgement reference.

data_elements.name: Assertion confidence qualifier
data_elements.description: Qualifier expressing how strongly the asserting agent stands behind the edge, distinguishing observed, inferred and declared assertions.

artifacts.name: Provenance and custody record
artifacts.description: Structured statement binding a dependency or impact record to its responsible agent, generating activity, derivation lineage, supporting evidence references with digests, and custody chain. It records claims; it performs no verification and grants no trust.
media_or_form: structured provenance record in any serialization
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by a minted UUIDv7 bound to the subject record digest and the generating activity reference; ordered by the activity's recorded end time.

layers.name: Operating Surface and Delegated Boundaries
layers.description: The interface-neutral declaration of what can be read, created, changed, projected and retired, and the explicit delegation of retention execution, access decisions and audit-trail ownership outside this model.

findings.name: Query, mutation and delegated retention, access and audit boundaries
findings.description: The operating surface is declared as capabilities, not endpoints: which selection expressions are supported and in what expression language, whether results are complete or truncated, which mutation operations are accepted and under what preconditions, and which projections are offered. Retirement of a record produces a tombstone that preserves the identifier, final digest, disposition reason and the policy reference authorising disposition, so that dangling references resolve to an explicit retired state rather than silently disappearing. Execution of erasure in downstream stores, the access decision itself, and the audit trail are owned by the adopting Dimension and the referenced retention, authorization and audit models; this model records the request, the reference and the outcome received, and never decides, enforces or stores the audit trail.

questions.text: Which query and mutation capabilities does this deployment declare, in which expression language, and with what completeness guarantee?
answer_data: Supported selection expression language and version
Supported mutation operations and their preconditions
Result completeness flag and truncation rule

answer_data: Retention class and minimum retention period
Governing retention policy reference held by the adopting Dimension
Executing party reference and confirmation-of-execution record reference

Final content digest and last valid version reference
Disposition reason, disposition timestamp and successor reference if any

answer_data: Policy reference and decision-point identifier held externally
Decision inputs this model exposes (sensitivity label, tenant partition, owner package)
Explicit statement that no decision or enforcement occurs here

answer_data: List of auditable operations
Minimum event fields to emit (operation, record identifier, version digests, actor reference, observation timestamp)
